chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Tamattu', so he said:

I said: He performed Hajj al-Qada (compensatory Hajj), that he had performed Hajj al-Tamattu' in that year or after it. I said: May Allah make you prosperous, I asked you and you ordered me to perform Tamattu', yet I see that you have performed Hajj al-Qada this year. He said: By Allah, the merit is in what I ordered you to do, but I am weak, so the two circumambulations (Tawaf) between As-Safa and Al-Marwah were difficult for me, therefore I performed Hajj al-Qada.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعِ: Hajj al-Tamattu' (a type of pilgrimage where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj in the same year)
key_terms.بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Between As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the site of the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.طَوَافَانِ: The two circumambulations (Tawaf al-Ifadah and Tawaf al-Qudum or similar, referring to the extra ritual effort)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam perform Hajj al-Qada instead of Hajj al-Tamattu' if he ordered others to do Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar highlights the distinction between the general ruling (hukm) and the Imam's personal preference (tarjih), demonstrating that while Hajj al-Tamattu' is superior, physical hardship can justify opting for Hajj al-Qada. It underscores the Shia principle of ease in religious obligations, showing the Imam's humility in admitting his own weakness despite his authoritative command. This context is vital for understanding how jurists derive rulings that account for individual capacity.
